findings.reason: The protected query is the canonical expert-interview solution: two exam-partitioned RANK windows mark every tied low and high score, one grouped student-history check rejects anyone with a rank-one row, and a final identity join produces the requested ordered output. The structure is concise, conventional, tie-safe, and directly explainable; no material improvement warrants a candidate.

Within each exam, ascending rank one identifies every row equal to the minimum and descending rank one identifies every row equal to the maximum. A student's grouped minimum rank in either direction equals one exactly when at least one participation is extreme. Requiring both minima above one therefore accepts precisely participating students whose complete histories contain no extremes; students without Exam rows never form a group.

An independent Python oracle computed each exam's minimum and maximum scores, collected all participating IDs, and removed every student matching either bound in any exam. It, the protected app query, exact immutable native query, a separately written extrema/anti-join control, and a correct de-indexed correlated-extrema control agreed exactly on all eight visible cases and all three benchmark tiers.

Seed 1412 generated 5,000 source-valid databases totaling 58,681 Exam rows and 8,067 quiet output rows. Coverage included 319 empty Student tables, 971 empty Exam tables, 1,940 databases with no-exam students, 3,292 single-participant exams, 256 all-equal multi-participant exams, 2,162 tied minima, 2,183 tied maxima, 3,279 with students taking several exams, 2,452 with quiet students, 3,833 with duplicate names, and shuffled rows; every implementation matched the oracle.

Across three real-test repetitions, the protected query passed all eight ordinary cases, all three benchmark outputs, and scaling with extra growth exponent -0.02 through +0.01 and largest-tier ratio 0.98x through 1.01x. The independent extrema control passed at -0.07 through -0.04 and 0.87x through 0.90x. The de-indexed correlated control passed every output but failed only scaling each time, at +0.86 through +0.88 and 8.73x through 9.73x.

All three benchmark cases remain explicitly hidden and performance-only, use positive unique sizes 48, 192, and 768 for a 16x span, and define size consistently as combined Student and Exam rows. Their 8/32/128 independent three-person exams force both rankings, grouped histories, and all middle-score outputs to grow together. Correct correlated extrema rescans repeatedly fail only growth, so benchmark.json was not edited.

The complete Approach now derives both window ranks, explains why RANK rather than ROW_NUMBER is required, proves the grouped-history condition in both directions, explains no-participation exclusion and the identity join, and states O(E log E + S) time and O(E + S) space. It covers extrema aggregation, correlated scans, tied extrema, all-equal and singleton exams, several exams, no participation, duplicate names, and ordering.

All eight ordinary cases are visible samples or trials. The sole authenticated source example remains exact with five Student rows, ten Exam rows, Jade as the only output, and the complete four-exam/no-participation explanation. Two invented samples are now trials, both formerly hidden cases are visible, and added trials cover tied maxima with a surviving middle score plus all scores tied at both extremes.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode database problem 1412 and SQL/MySQL as the native environment. The query respects the Student primary key, Exam composite primary key, exam-local scores, at-least-one-exam requirement, complete-history quantifier, tied minima and maxima, singleton exams, the two requested source columns, and ascending student_id order.

The protected app-local sql.sql and immutable leetcode.sql bound to verified submission 2069002090 are canonically identical and remain byte-for-byte unchanged, as does submission.json. solution_variants.json continues to select that protected source, no candidate exists, and no remote-Accepted evidence was altered or inferred.

A fresh authenticated Premium review confirmed both table schemas and primary keys, exam-score row meaning, quiet-student and at-least-one-exam rules, complete-history requirement, two requested columns, ascending output order, one exact example with its full per-exam explanation, five source tables, and no separate constraints, hints, notes, images, diagrams, or follow-up. source_fidelity.json binds five modular Reference files to live-content SHA-256 eb83255e5ea20b20d0491ccd2a0a05a2da28c28a4a7e77a06b74ae78491956fa and validates without errors.
